text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Newcastle United and Burnley at St James' Park.
The hosts come into this game on a high looking to extend their unbeaten run to five matches after a brilliant couple of weeks that have included some eye-catching results.
They beat Brentford at home before picking up a solid point away at Milan to open their Champions League campaign.
There were no signs of a European hangover as they demolished Sheffield United 8-0 last weekend, before dumping treble winners Manchester City out of the EFL Cup in midweek.
Burnley picked up a confidence-boosting 4-0 thrashing of League Two side Salford City in the EFL Cup on Tuesday, a much-needed distraction after a poor start to their Premier League return.
They are yet to win a league game and are only kept off the bottom of the table thanks to their superior goal difference over the Blades.
Vincent Kompany will be keen to use their cup success in midweek to try and finally put their first three points on the board in the league.
Eddie Howe makes eight changes from the cup win over City with only Pope, Lascelles and Isak retaining their places, with the latter of that trio scoring the winner in that game.
The likes of Trippier and Guimaraes return, while the in-form Gordon will start on the left wing.
Howe has injury worries with Callum Wilson, Sven Botman and Harvey Barnes all ruled out of this one.
Kompany also brings back the majority of his first-choice starting XI after ringing the changes against Salford with Berge the only one to keep his place.
Trafford returns between the sticks while Amdouni is preferred to Rodriguez up top.
Cullen and Koleosho are among those to come back into the side.
The two sets of players make their way onto the pitch and we are moments away from kick-off!
The visitors get us underway at St James' Park!
Newcastle are doing most of the early pressing here as they look to get off to a quick start.
BIG CHANCE! A huge opportunity goes begging for the visitors as a Burn slip allows Koleosho to nip in.
The winger drives into the box before squaring for Amdouni, but Pope bails out his defender as he makes a great stop with his right foot to deny Amdouni's goalbound effort.
Newcastle have won their last four Premier League games against Burnley, as many as they had in their previous 15 league meetings with the Clarets (five draws, six defeats).
Kompany's men are looking a threat when they come forward, with Koleosho causing Burn a few issues down Newcastle's left.
Brownhill is perhaps a bit fortunate not to receive an early booking after he clattered into Gordon.
A stray pass in the Burnley defence is latched onto by Guimaraes, who immediately looks for Isak.
The striker receives the ball before making space for a shot, but his eventual effort is saved down low by Trafford.
Burnley are winless in their last nine away league games against Newcastle (four draws, five losses) since a 1-0 victory in April 1976.
They would love to end that shocking run here.
GOAL!!! ALMIRON SCORES A STUNNER!!! Ramsey takes far too much time with the ball at his feet in a dangerous area, and Trippier manages to nip it away from him and into the path of Almiron.
The Paraguay international then charges forward, before setting his sights on the top left corner.
His strike is then excellent, curling over Trafford and in to put Newcastle 1-0 up!
Trippier dispossessed Ramsey and found Almiron in the process, before his team-mate superbly arrowed home.
That was Trippier's fourth assist of the Premier League season, the most in the division.
Gordon receives the first booking of the contest for kicking the ball away.
Longstaff pulls a shot well wide of the target as he drags a bouncing ball past the left post.
The Clarets are struggling to get a foothold in this game at the minute, with their hosts looking the much more likely side to grab the second goal of the contest.
Newcastle won 8-0 against the Blades in their last Premier League game, their biggest ever away league win and biggest overall since 1999, an 8-0 home win over Sheffield Wednesday.
They had eight different scorers in the match, a new record by a team in a single Premier League match (excluding own goals).
WHAT A CHANCE! Guimaraes' excellent first-time throughball puts Isak in, but Trafford races out to close him down.
The ball comes off the Burnley goalkeeper and loops into the air, and it just will not come down quickly enough for the striker as he ends up off balance, flicking wide of the left post.
Amdouni is booked after a very late challenge on Almiron.
Just over half an hour in at St James' Park and Newcastle have largely been in control.
Howe will be keen for a second goal though to tighten his side's grip on the game.
For a fifth time in their nine Premier League seasons, Burnley have failed to win any of their opening five matches.
The only side to do so in more different campaigns in the competition is Newcastle (seven).
INCREDIBLE SAVE! Trafford makes a world-class stop to deny Anderson.
Longstaff lofts a deep cross to the back post for his fellow Newcastle academy product, and it looks for all the world as if Anderson is going to nod the Magpies two goals ahead.
However, Trafford somehow manages to keep it out before his defenders scramble clear.
Burnley's last shot in this game came back in the fourth minute.
They have really struggled to create anything of note since Almiron's opening goal.
Beyer is booked for a cynical pull on Isak.
The Sweden international and the home crowd are frustrated at the referee's decision not to play advantage with the striker bearing down on goal.
We are nearing the interval, and Kompany will be keen to get his team back to the changing rooms to try and find a way back into this game.
The hosts have been by far the better team so far, though their lead remains a slender one.
Amdouni sees a shot blocked wide by Longstaff as Burnley finally have their first shot since the fourth minute.
The corner then comes to nothing.
We are into two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Trafford gives the ball away in a terrible area but makes up for his mistake by getting down low to save Anderson's curling effort after a neat one-two with Almiron made the space.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-0 BURNLEY
The teams head back to the changing rooms with the hosts 1-0 up at St James' Park thanks to Almiron's opening goal.
Burnley could have been ahead just four minutes in after Burn's slip let Koleosho in to square for Amdouni, though Pope made a great stop to deny the forward's low shot.
The Clarets were made to pay for that miss with 14 minutes gone, Trippier dispossessing Ramsey before Almiron took full advantage by sending a delightful curling finish into the back of the net.

Isak could and probably should have made it 2-0 when he shot wide, while Trafford made a sublime stop to somehow stop Anderson's diving header flying in to ensure his side went into the break just the one goal down.
Newcastle have been much the better team, but their advantage is only a single goal and Kompany will know his side still have a chance.
Howe will be looking for what could be a decisive second goal and has a very strong bench to call upon if he needs, with the likes of Tonali and Joelinto among the substitutes.
The Magpies get us back underway for the second period.
CLOSE! Beyer's header to clear a cross only finds Trippier near the edge of the box.
The full-back brings it down before rifling towards goal, and his shot takes a wicked deflection off Taylor.
Burnley's hearts are in mouths as the ball goes goalwards, though fortunately for them, the nick only sends the ball just wide of the post.
Burnley have lost all four of the Premier League games in which they have been trailing at half-time this season.
Kompany will be looking for a better response from his team.
Trippier and Ramsey clash in midfield after the Burnley man brought down the right-back.
The referee manages to quickly calm things down, though.
A deep cross comes off a Burnley head and reaches Schar at the back post, but the centre-back's touch gets away from him and the ball runs out for a goal-kick.
Taylor receives a yellow card for a very heavy sliding challenge on Trippier, who is not best pleased with the tackle.
Longstaff gets up well to meet Trippier's cross, but he cannot hit the target with his header as it flies high and wide of Trafford's goal.
Trippier whips another teasing delivery into the Burnley penalty area, but it just evades Isak in the middle.
Newcastle are still looking the more threatening, and Kompany looks as if he is going to go to his bench to try and change that.
Kompany makes a pair of changes.
The first sees Bruun Larsen come on for Koleosho.
Rodriguez also enters the fray in place of Amdouni.
Half an hour remaining at St James' Park and despite Newcastle's dominance, their lead remains a narrow one.
Kompany will be looking for his substitutes to bring more attacking threat and offer a way back into the contest, while Howe will be desperate for a second goal to potentially put this game to bed.
Burnley have only accumulated 0.49 xG (expected goals), 0.4 of which came from Amdouni's fourth-minute effort that was saved by Pope.
Howe makes his first alteration, bringing on Joelinton for Anderson.
Just minutes after coming on, Joelinton pulls up before going down in the Burnley box.
This would be a big blow for Howe and Newcastle.
Ramsey makes way for Odobert.
Joelinton is forced off.
Tonali comes on in his place.

Of the 13 previous instances of a team scoring eight goals in a Premier League match, only one has then gone on and lost their next match (W9 D3) – that was Newcastle in September 1999 against Leeds United.

None have ever failed to score in their next game, with Liverpool in September 1989 the last to do that in the top-flight, following up a 9-0 win over Crystal Palace with a 0-0 draw with Norwich City.
A couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession come to nothing as they press for a second goal that will likely put this game beyond Burnley's reach.
PENALTY TO NEWCASTLE!!! Gordon takes the ball past Al Dakhil in the Burnley penalty area and the centre-back goes diving in.
It is a rash challenge, and the referee points straight to the spot.
The hosts will have a huge opportunity to double their lead!
GOAL!!! Cool as you like, Isak steps up and sends Trafford the wrong way, stroking into the bottom right corner to put Newcastle 2-0 up and surely on the way to another three points.
A rare foray forward for Burnley ends with Odobert firing towards goal, though his shot is blocked wide for a corner.
Looking to make up for his mistake for the penalty, Al Dakhil nods goalwards from a corner.
It looks to be going over, but Pope tips it over anyway just to be sure.
Howe's men are looking for a third goal, though their opponents are able to clear a couple of corners into their box, keeping themselves in the game.
Guimaraes cleverly wins a free-kick in midfield as he teases Cullen into a challenge.
Newcastle have looked the smarter, more experienced side in this game.
Burnley have had just two shots on target in this match, compared to seven for their opponents.
They have just not been able to make a dent on their hosts.
Berge makes way for Vitinho.
Zaroury comes on for Berge.
Trafford makes another save to deny Isak from a tight angle as we move into six minutes of additional time.
Can the Clarets force a grandstand finish?
Burnley are looking a defeated side now.
Their opponents are knocking the ball around nicely, and Kompany's men are struggling to get hold of possession.
Newcastle have had five big chances in this game, compared to just one for their opponents.
The Magpies have been the much more threatening side.
Howe makes a couple of changes in the dying seconds, as Almiron makes way for Murphy.
Isak is replaced by Livramento.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-0 BURNLEY
The full-time whistle blows as Newcastle run out comfortable 2-0 victors after a solid display at St James' Park.

They were nearly behind after just four minutes when Pope denied Amdouni, but the hosts dominated from that point on and took the lead with 14 minutes gone, Trippier taking the ball off Ramsey high up the pitch before Almiron arrowed home a superb finish.

Howe's men struggled to find a second goal to kill the game off, but any potential for late nerves was banished 14 minutes from time as Isak coolly stroked home a penalty after Al Dakhil's rash challenge on Gordon.
The visitors struggled to create much all game, and Newcastle easily saw out the remaining minutes for another three points.
The Magpies now unbeaten in five, moving them into the top half of the Premier League.
They now turn their attentions to the Champions League with a huge clash with Kylian Mbappe and Paris Saint-Germain to come on Wednesday when they host the Ligue 1 champions at St James' Park.
For Burnley, their dismal start continues, though they remain above the Blades after the Yorkshire side were beaten 2-0 away at West Ham.
They travel to Luton Town on Tuesday looking to claim what could be a big three points against another side expected to be among those looking to avoid relegation.
Thanks for joining us for live coverage of Newcastle United's 2-0 Premier League victory over Burnley at St James' Park.
Goodbye!
